CNBC China-EU hybrid vehicle export deal (second outlet)

 - BEIJING — European trade commissioner Maroš Sefčovič said Friday that China has agreed to halve its exports of hybrid cars to the bloc.
 - Europe has called on China to voluntarily reduce hybrid car exports into the continent, but authorities in Beijing had reportedly slapped down the request, according to the Financial Times.
 - The widening trade surplus between the EU and China has been a point of contention, with Germany and France previously having called on Brussels to develop a "last-resort" trade instrument to address imbalances.
 - Sefčovič said Friday that the final decision would still need Brussels' approval. Overall, he cast the two days of talks with China's Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing as a positive first step, following a summer of rising tensions between China and the EU.
 - China's Commerce Ministry on Friday released a list of 16 "'consensus outcomes."
 - They included licenses for rare earth and permanent magnet export licenses to the EU. Sefcovic did not elaborate on a timeline for the rare earth exports.
 - Earlier this year, on June 29 for the first meeting of the EU-China Trade and Investment Consultations.
 - The two sides agreed to next meet in March, with a video conference in January, according to the Chinese readout.
